messages:
maria: Heads-up — Windows users (embeddable Python + 3.10/3.11) seeing intermittent SSL cert verification failures when creating the Python SDK client. Happens in CI and on-dev machines. Full minimal trace below. Anyone seen a precedence bug between REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and SSL_CERT_FILE on Windows?

maria: ```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 12, in <module>
    client = RedwoodClient(api_key=... )
  File ".../redwood/client.py", line 45, in __init__
    resp = requests.get("https://api.redwood.ai/health")
  File "C:\\hosted\\lib\\ssl.py", line 123, in wrap_socket
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:XXXX)
```

ben: Which Python build? windows embeddable often has no cert store + different OpenSSL.

maria: Embeddable zip from python.org, unpacked into dev VM. Not using system python.

carla: Yep — embeddable doesn't ship with certs by default. Most folks fix by installing certifi and setting SSL_CERT_FILE or REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE. But note: different libs look at different env vars. :grimacing:

carla: Quick workaround I use: ```python
import os, certifi
os.environ.setdefault('SSL_CERT_FILE', certifi.where())
# then import requests / redwood client
```

sam: Important: aiohttp / asyncio stacks sometimes bypass REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and consult ssl.create_default_context(cafile=...). If SDK has async client code that builds its own context, env vars won't help. We should ensure the SDK's async path respects certifi by default.

ben: Can you repro with a tiny script? If yes, paste pip freeze + minimal script.

maria: Minimal repro attached: ```python
# repro.py
import os
import certifi
os.environ.pop('SSL_CERT_FILE', None)
# no cert env set
from redwood import Client
Client(api_key='x')
```

maria: pip freeze: certifi==2023.11.7, requests==2.31.0, aiohttp==3.8.4, redwood==0.12.1

andy: I hit something similar — REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE worked for requests but grpc/vendored ssl didn't pick it up. On Windows we ended up setting SSL_CERT_FILE globally to certifi.where().

carla: Another gotcha: `setx` vs `set` (session vs persistent). For CI you want to set the env before the process starts, e.g.:
```
pip install certifi
setx SSL_CERT_FILE "%PYTHONHOME%\\Lib\\site-packages\\certifi\\cacert.pem"
```
Works around embeddable distro lacking cert store.

sam: Actionable SDK fix: if no explicit ssl context provided, construct one with certifi.where() as cafile for both sync and async clients. That should make embeddable and weird Windows builds behave without extra env config. File an issue/PR?

maria: Filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/issues/1234 — summary + repro + suggested change.

devx-bot: Reference docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/python#ssl-and-windows (TODO: expand w/ certifi example) :link:

ben: Small patch suggestion in comment — check for env or certifi and fallback gracefully. Also add a debug log when we fallback so users can see why certs were chosen.

carla: Agree — add tests for embeddable Python and a CI matrix job for Windows embeddable if possible.

maria: Thanks all — workarounds posted in the issue. I can pick the SDK change if maintainers 👍. :thumbsup:

andy: Verified after setting SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi.where(), repro stops.

maria: Closing loop — putting short note in onboarding doc about Windows embeddable and certs.

ben: Nice. Might also add a one-liner in quickstart to run `python -m certifi` or set env.

maria: yea, and we'll make the SDK do the right thing by default (PR incoming). :rocket:
